newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian government vows to pay striking teachers.
newsitem.headline: Russian government vows to pay striking teachers.

text.p: The Russian government promised on Thursday to pay the wages owed to teachers who have been on strike all week.

Russian news agencies quoted first deputy finance minister Andrei Petrov as saying all back wages would be paid to teachers and university staff by the end of January. Students would also receive money owed to them from their grants.
"The (wage) debt will be wiped out by the end of January," Interfax news agency quoted Petrov as telling a government meeting.
Union leaders said 437,000 teachers were now on strike demanding their salaries and that the protests had affected more than 10,000 schools and three million pupils.
Some teachers, like many other public sector workers, say they have not been paid for months.

The government, struggling with a shortfall in tax revenues, has also promised to end delays in paying wages to other public sector workers following a series of strikes, but many workers remain without their salaries.
